## Clean notebook imports in one command

Imports and installation commands often end up scattered across an exploratory
notebook. Notebook Cell Organizer moves top-level imports and shell commands to
dedicated cells at the beginning of the notebook without moving conditional or
function-local imports.

::: {.demo-frame}
![Notebook Cell Organizer reorganizing a Jupyter notebook in VS Code](assets/demo.gif){fig-alt="VS Code extension collecting imports and shell commands into dedicated Jupyter notebook cells"}
:::

::: {.feature-grid}
::: {.feature-card}
### Collect imports

Moves top-level `import` and `from ... import ...` statements into one import
cell, including parenthesized multi-line imports.
:::

::: {.feature-card}
### Sort with Ruff

Optionally runs Ruff's import rules on the collected Python imports. The command
and arguments are configurable for `uv`, virtual environments, and custom setups.
:::

::: {.feature-card}
### Preserve behavior

Leaves imports inside `TYPE_CHECKING`, conditionals, `try` blocks, functions,
and classes exactly where they are.
:::

::: {.feature-card}
### Remove repetition

Deduplicates repeated imports and shell commands while removing cells that
become empty after organization.
:::

::: {.feature-card}
### Organize on save

Use the notebook toolbar or Command Palette, or enable automatic organization
whenever a notebook is saved.
:::

::: {.feature-card}
### Fail safely

If Ruff is unavailable or fails, the extension keeps the collected imports and
finishes the basic organization.
:::
:::

## Before and after

::: {.comparison-grid}
::: {.comparison-card}
### Before

```python
# cell 0
import pandas as pd
data = pd.read_csv("data.csv")

# cell 1
import os
!pip install scikit-learn
```
:::

::: {.comparison-card}
### After

```python
# cell 0
!pip install scikit-learn

# cell 1
import os

import pandas as pd

# cell 2
data = pd.read_csv("data.csv")
```
:::
:::

## Get started

1. Install [Notebook Cell Organizer from the VS Code Marketplace](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=showpiecep.notebook-cell-organizer).
2. Open a Jupyter Notebook in VS Code.
3. Open the Command Palette and run **Notebook: Organize Notebook Cells**, or use the notebook toolbar button.
4. Optionally [enable Ruff import sorting](ruff.qmd).

No Ruff installation is required for the standard organizer.
